about: The context quiz: questions the head trader (and the risk manager) must answer from their prompts alone, each the agreed rule it checks and the phrase in the skills that states it. Run on demand (scripts/context-quiz.js), never in CI: it calls a model. A changed key or question needs a reason in the pull request, as a golden does.
answerFormat: Answer from your instructions only. First line: ANSWER: <one line>. Then at most 3 lines of why.
unsure: it depends|unsure|not sure|unclear|ambiguous|can't tell|cannot tell|depends on

questions.text: The 4h trend is up and the 1h trend is down. Can you take a long? A short?
questions.rule: no side when the 4h and 1h disagree: never counter
questions.anchor: each trending 4h or 1h your way, neither against

questions.text: The 4h and 1h both range. What sets the side?
questions.rule: both ranging: the 15m trend and the declared trend
questions.anchor: both ranging: the 15m and `Trend declared?` your way

questions.text: The 4h is down, the 1h down, and a 1h CHoCH up just printed at a level. Can you go long?
questions.rule: never against a trending 4h or 1h; a CHoCH against the bias is context
questions.anchor: A CHoCH against the bias is context, never a way in.

questions.text: Which timeframes set the bias?
questions.rule: the bias is the 4h and the 1h
questions.anchor: The bias (4h + 1h) sets the side

questions.text: Which timeframe is the setup read on?
questions.rule: the setup is the 15m (or a fired momentum_continuation)
questions.anchor: The setup is the 15m (or higher) reaction or break

questions.text: What is a 3m swing high for: a level to trade from, a target, or only where the stop goes?
questions.rule: a 3m swing is no level and no target, only where the stop goes
questions.anchor: A 3m swing is not a level and not a target.

questions.text: A 3m CHoCH up prints while the 15m setup has not formed. Is that a setup?
questions.rule: a 3m break is never the setup
questions.anchor: a 3m candle is no setup

questions.text: A 15m setup candle closed as a bearish engulfing; another closed as a strong full-body bear candle in its bottom third with no pattern name. Which is the stronger setup candle?
questions.rule: a candle is judged by its strength and close, never its pattern name
questions.anchor: a name adds no strength, the reaction reads who took control

questions.text: Where do levels come from?
questions.rule: levels: the 1h and higher, the session and day, the VWAP, the 15m swings; never the 3m
questions.anchor: Levels come from the 1h and higher, the session and day

questions.text: The 15m setup closed at a 1h level on the bias side. When do you enter?
questions.rule: the next 3m close times the entry; no 3m turn to wait for
questions.anchor: no 3m turn to wait for

questions.text: Do you need a 3m BOS or CHoCH before entering?
questions.rule: no 3m break is required
questions.anchor: no 3m turn or break to wait for

questions.text: No size fits under the cap with compose's stop. Do you tighten the stop?
questions.rule: stops are locked: skip, never a tighter stop
questions.anchor: pass, never a closer stop

questions.text: Where does the stop go?
questions.rule: compose places the stop one tick beyond the named level; never tighter; on the bracket
questions.anchor: The stop: compose places it one tick beyond the level your stop read

questions.text: Can you move the stop to breakeven because the trade feels done?
questions.rule: the stop moves only behind turned structure (the trail)
questions.anchor: You tighten it only behind

questions.text: The trade reaches 2R. Do you exit there?
questions.rule: at 2R nothing exits: the 2R order is cancelled, the stop locks and trails
questions.anchor: At 2R nothing exits

questions.text: Is the named 1h swing high your exit?
questions.rule: the trail exits; a level is context
questions.anchor: the 2R mark that arms the trail, not the exit

questions.text: In a prop attempt the account is healthy (balance at or above start, no loss streak). What size: the full verdict size, or less?
questions.rule: a healthy prop account takes the full verdict size
questions.anchor: Size in a prop attempt: the full verdict size, the code's number.

questions.text: The setup has one serious factor against it, in a prop attempt. What size: the full verdict size, or less?
questions.rule: in a prop attempt nothing halves
questions.anchor: In a prop attempt nothing halves

questions.text: The risk manager writes "Size: I'd go with 3 contracts given the stop" and "VERDICT: approve". Is that a trade?
questions.rule: a bare approval states no readable size: one restate of the Size and VERDICT lines, never a veto (roles-ran.js approvedSize)
questions.anchor: with no size on the line → unreadable

questions.text: The setup fits only 2 contracts at the stop. What do you do?
questions.rule: fewer than the minimum (3) at the stop: skip, unless the code's floor stretch fits it
questions.anchor: Fewer than 3 (`min_contracts`) at the stop: skip

questions.text: Positions read flat, but a fill shows a long 9 and its bracket stop is working. Do you cancel the stop as a leftover?
questions.rule: a fill reported late: a stop is never a leftover while fills or an order's status show the position; keep it ([cancel-protection] refuses its cancel)
questions.anchor: A stop is never a leftover while fills or an order's status show the position, even if positions read flat: `[cancel-protection]` refuses it; keep it.

questions.text: In a prop attempt your compose record states 8 MNQ, but order_plan gives 5 MNQ for the entry. What size do you place?
questions.rule: the size comes from the size translation (order_plan's number), never the model's own
questions.anchor: size, and stop ticks come from the size translation (`order_plan` gives them)

questions.text: A 15m long-wick rejection at the prior RTH high, nothing else lines up. Take it on the reaction alone?
questions.rule: a reaction is context, never decided on alone: it needs other confirmation (the bias, the level, the count)
questions.anchor: Context, never the setup alone: it needs other confirmation.

questions.text: A 15m candle has a long upper wick above the prior RTH high but closes above the high. Rejection or acceptance?
questions.rule: the close decides acceptance, the wick measures the failed attempt: a close beyond the level is acceptance, never a rejection
questions.anchor: The close beats the wick: a long wick closing above is no rejection

questions.text: A 15m candle trades above the prior RTH high and closes back below it, its upper wick longer than its body and a third of its range (the briefing: long-wick rejection). Who took control?
questions.rule: a long-wick rejection after a high: the other side, the sellers, took control
questions.anchor: → sellers rejected higher prices

questions.text: A 15m candle trades above the prior RTH high and closes above it, its body 0.8 of its range. A sweep of the high or a breakout?
questions.rule: a close beyond with an engulfing or a body of 0.7 of the range or more is a breakout attempt, not a sweep
questions.anchor: the breaking side in control, not a sweep

questions.text: A 15m long-wick rejection of the prior RTH high, then the next 15m candle is a bearish engulfing closing lower. What does that second candle read?
questions.rule: a long-wick rejection, then an opposite engulfing closing lower: a confirmed rejection, on the second candle
questions.anchor: closing lower → sellers took over, confirmed

questions.text: A 15m candle trades above the prior RTH high and closes back below it with a bullish body and a short wick (the briefing: conflicting). Read it as sellers in control now?
questions.rule: a conflicting reaction is mixed evidence: it needs other confirmation (the count, or the next candle)
questions.anchor: → mixed: needs other confirmation (the count, or the next candle)

questions.text: A 15m doji at the prior RTH high (the briefing: stall). What decides who takes control?
questions.rule: a stall: the push stalled, the next candle decides
questions.anchor: → stalled; the next candle decides

questions.text: Two 15m long-wick rejections of a high (upper wick through it, closed back below): one at a pullback level with the 4h and 1h down, one with the 4h and 1h up. What side is each, and which can be taken?
questions.rule: the side is the candle's: both are the short side (a rejection of a high); only the first, with the 4h and 1h, can be taken; against the 4h + 1h the trend rule refuses the second (never counter)
questions.anchor: Side first, from the candle

questions.text: The last 4h candle is a long-wick rejection of the prior RTH high; the 15m candle at it reads plain. Which reaction is the stronger, and is it a trade on its own?
questions.rule: the reaction rules hold on every timeframe and a higher frame's reaction is stronger confirmation than a lower one's; a reaction is still context: it needs other confirmation
questions.anchor: a higher frame's reaction is stronger confirmation than a lower one's
required: \b(needs?|wants?|requires?)\s+(other|more)\s+confirmation\b|\bconfirmation\b|\bcontext\b|\bthe count\b|\bnot (a trade )?(on its own|alone|by itself)\b|\bneither( one)? is a trade\b|\bis not a trade\b
forbidden: \b(trade it|sell it|go short|enter now|stands on its own|tradeable on its own|(valid|good) trade (by itself|on its own))\b(?!\s+(only\s+)?(once|if|after(?! all)|when|until)\b)

questions.text: The 3m candle is a long-wick rejection of the prior RTH high, but the last 1h candle closed decisively beyond it (broke above). Short on the 3m rejection?
questions.rule: a higher frame's reaction is stronger confirmation than a lower one's: the 1h close beyond outweighs the 3m rejection; the 3m only times the entry and alone can be noise (wait)
questions.anchor: 3m only times the entry; alone it can be noise

questions.text: Two 15m long-wick rejections of a low (lower wick through it, closed back above): one at a pullback level with the 4h and 1h up, one with the 4h and 1h down. What side is each, and which can be taken?
questions.rule: the side is the candle's: both are the long side (a rejection of a low); only the first, with the 4h and 1h, can be taken; against the 4h + 1h the trend rule refuses the second (never counter)
questions.anchor: Side first, from the candle

questions.text: A 15m candle `rejected` the prior RTH high (traded above, closed back below), and its reaction reads plain. Did the other side take control — is it a rejection?
questions.rule: the `rejected` relation is only the fact; it is a rejection only when its reaction is a long-wick, engulfing or confirmed rejection; plain: no one took control, weak context only
questions.anchor: It is a rejection only when its reaction is a long-wick, engulfing or confirmed rejection
required: \b(not a rejection|no rejection|no one took control|nobody took control|weak|context|confirm\w*|by itself|alone|reaction decides)\b
forbidden: \b(short it|take the short|go short|sell it)\b(?!\s+(only\s+)?(once|if|after(?! all)|when|until)\b)

questions.text: A 15m candle `rejected` a level in your composed read and its reaction reads conflicting. Which skill do you read for what that means, and how?
questions.rule: the reaction read is candle-reading's, read from the index with skill_lookup (or the cycle's embedded copy); the gate requires it on a composed rejection or break
questions.anchor: - a composed read says a candle rejected a level, or a composed read says a candle broke a level, or a composed read says a level was swept: `candle-reading`

questions.text: In a prop attempt, momentum_continuation fired long on the BG side. Can you take it?
questions.rule: a cited setup (S2) is traded in the attempt: cite it in compose_check (trade_lifecycle's citedSetup), never a reason to pass for being a rules strategy
questions.anchor: A setup the prompt names in this attempt (S2): cite it in

questions.text: The fired setup's track record says no backtest recorded. Is that a reason to pass?
questions.rule: a missing track record is never a reason to pass or cut (trade_lifecycle and a cited setup have none)
questions.anchor: never a reason to pass or cut

partB.text: A 15m bullish CHoCH prints at the prior VAL. Trade it long?
partB.rule: the Bias line refuses the long

partB.text: A 15m rejection up at the VWAP. Which side, if any?
partB.rule: the Bias line gives the long

partB.text: A 15m CISD up at a 1h level. Trade it?
One serious factor against the setup. What size: the full verdict size, or less?
partB.rule: the Size line: the full verdict

partB.text: The cap fits only 2 contracts at the stop. Take it with 2?
